messages:
maria_cs: Pinwheel reporting lots of 429s on SDK init during a nighttime canary. Spike ~400 in 30s in eu-west.

maria_cs: snippet they pasted: ```POST /v1/sdk/init  HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
x-request-id: pin-err-214
Response: 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
```

pinwheel-ops: We use the default browser bootstrapper and rotate ephemeral tokens aggressively. Current config: `ephemeralTTL: 12` and no init jitter.

sam_sdk: Quick customer guidance: 1) increase ephemeralTTL to 120-300s, 2) add a randomized splay on app start, 3) ensure keepAlive/proxy reuse at the edge so you don't open 400 new connections.

jules_eng: Infra note: auth validation QPS for their account jumped and auth queue backlog spiked. Short-term we can enable a request-coalescing flag for their account to dedupe identical token validations for 20s.

infra-guy: I'll toggle the flag for a 15 minute window and watch metrics. ETA ~10m.

onboard-bot: Ticket CS-#4992 created: "Pinwheel SDK init 429s (canary)". Assigned to jules_eng, infra-guy.

pinwheel-ops: We'll flip TTL to 180 on a 5% canary and add a 200-800ms client jitter. Rolling slowly.

maria_cs: Please collect any x-request-id samples if 429s persist so we can trace to the auth queue.

sam_sdk: Long-term SDK change: add `initSplayMs` + `ephemeralDefault` options and doc the recommended rollout pattern (10% -> 50% -> 100% with client jitter). I'll file an RFC.

maria_cs: Thanks. Logging into customer health and will follow up after the canary. :white_check_mark:
